thread:
alex: :rotating_light: apiserver 502s in ap-southeast-1 since ~04:03 UTC. controller-manager started retrying leader election, a few pods stuck Terminating. seeing a spike in GPU attach errors around same time. logs: `Post "/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods": dial tcp 10.50.3.12:6443: connect: connection refused`

maria: confirmed, dashboards show apiserver fd usage near 90% and pod attach latency P99 jumped to 12s. also NAT SNAT ephemeral ports climbing on the node pool.

kevin: any recent config changes? CNI or MTU?

nina: nothing intentional. but we rolled a GPU image update earlier and scaled the gpu-nodepool to recover capacity after churn. could be connection fanout from attach controller.

alex: hypothesis: attach controller retries + kube-proxy SNAT exhaustion -> connection failures to apiserver -> leader election flaps. can we verify SNAT table?

maria: running `kubectl -n kube-system exec -it node-exporter-xx -- ss -s` shows many TIME-WAIT and ephemeral port usage ~47k/64k.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-174. Pager duty notified.

kevin: workaround: reduce attach concurrency: patch controller-manager deployment to set `--leader-elect-lease-duration=15s`? that won't reduce load. better: throttle CSI attach controller by setting `--controllers=*,!attachdetach` temporarily. thoughts?

nina: we can flip attachcontroller off for a minute, but risk left-over volumes. prefer throttling by scaling down GPU nodepool autoscaler to stop new attaches for now.

alex: alternative immediate mitigations: 1) add more SNATports via iptables `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`? 2) increase kube-apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` lower to reduce fd pressure? 3) ensure kube-proxy isn't in legacy IPVS mode creating extra conntrack.

maria: I can bump conntrack on nodes to 262144 quickly: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and restart kube-proxy on affected nodes. doing that now.

kevin: while maria does that, I'll scale the GPU ASG down 20% to stop new attach churn. patching autoscaler.

alex: grabbing tcpdump on one node to check MTU-related fragmentation: `tcpdump -i eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/attach.pcap port 6443 or port 5471`

nina: note: we saw a few kernel dmesg lines earlier like `NETDEV WATCHDOG` on a subset of nodes — might be underlying host NIC driver instability after the GUImage update.

maria: conntrack increased, restarting kube-proxy pods one by one. ephemeral ports usage dropping by about 6k already.

ops-bot: Action log: conntrack tuned, gpu nodepool scale request submitted.

kevin: after scale-down, new attach attempts dropped to near zero. apiserver 502s reduced but not gone. leader election still jittery.

alex: suspect MTU mismatch between host and overlay causing retransmits & head-of-line blocking for kube-apiserver traffic. please check overlay MTU on nodes and the VPC route table for jumbo frames.

maria: confirmed two nodes show eth0 mtu 9000 while CNI app expects 1400. that matches the fragmentation symptoms. CNI's vxlan header + host mtu > path MTU -> large packets getting dropped.

nina: reverting MTU to 1400 on those hosts now: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400`. doing one at a time.

alex: once MTU fixed, watch apiserver fd and leader elections. if stable, we can roll remaining hosts. also create a short runbook step to validate MTU post-node-update.

maria: apiserver fd usage falling back to ~55%, leader election stabilized after ~90s, controller-manager leader regained. pod terminations progressing.

kevin: good. followups: 1) investigate why worker image set mtu 9000 (ci change?), 2) add conntrack and ephemeral port alerts, 3) add prescale logic in autoscaler to avoid simultaneous attach storms.

nina: logging a postmortem ticket with root cause draft: CI image changed host networking default mtu=9000 -> mismatch with VPC and CNI -> packet drops -> connection retransmits -> SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion + kube-apiserver fd pressure -> leader election churn + controller-manager retries -> visible 502s and pod Terminating.

alex: assign owners: maria for conntrack/apiserver tuning and alerting, kevin for autoscaler changes, nina for postmortem and CI fix. I'll open the RFC to avoid future host-level network surprises.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook suggestion: add MTU check to node health probe and a preflight on image bake. See: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mtu-check

alex: great. thanks everyone :thumbsup: closing this thread once PMs ack the followups.
